subject: Re: Kickoff: cognate reflex prediction for low-resource lexicons
body:
Hi both,

Reproduction status: the Neighbors model matches the shared-task submissions. The per-language mockingbird-n1 configs at 25k, 30k, and 100k steps line up with the released numbers, and the 100k run is the best of the three on most languages. The per-language-group n2 variant is close behind at a fraction of the training cost — one model per family instead of one per language.

The inpainting model (mockingbird-i1) is the concern: it reproduces, but it degrades badly on families where the cognate table is sparse, which is precisely our low-resource product case. Neighbors handles sparsity better because it conditions on whatever neighbors exist.

Risk/trade-off to settle in June: n1 quality vs n2 operational simplicity. Katya's head-to-head runs will decide it.

Wei
